question: How many customers are there?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM customers

question: List the names and prices of vegetarian menu items that cost more than 300, most expensive first.
gold_sql: SELECT item_name, price FROM menu_items WHERE is_veg = 1 AND price > 300 ORDER BY price DESC
notes: ordered by price descending; prices are all distinct

question: List the full names of delivery partners who are active and use a Bike.
gold_sql: SELECT full_name FROM delivery_partners WHERE is_active = 1 AND vehicle_type = 'Bike'

question: How many orders have been cancelled?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'Cancelled'

question: What is the name and price of the most expensive menu item?
gold_sql: SELECT item_name, price FROM menu_items ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 1
notes: single row; the maximum price is unique

question: For every delivered order, list the order ID and the name of the restaurant it was placed at.
gold_sql: SELECT o.order_id, r.name FROM orders o JOIN restaurants r ON o.restaurant_id = r.restaurant_id WHERE o.order_status = 'Delivered'

question: List each customer's full name together with the city of their default address.
gold_sql: SELECT c.full_name, a.city FROM customers c JOIN customer_addresses a ON a.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE a.is_default = 1
notes: default address = customer_addresses.is_default = 1

question: What is the full name of the customer who placed order 25?
gold_sql: SELECT c.full_name FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_id = 25

question: List the item names and category names of all menu items offered by the restaurant named 'Spice Symphony'.
gold_sql: SELECT m.item_name, c.category_name FROM menu_items m JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = m.category_id JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = m.restaurant_id WHERE r.name = 'Spice Symphony'
notes: three-table join

question: List the distinct vegetarian menu items (item name and restaurant name) that appear in delivered orders.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT m.item_name, r.name FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN menu_items m ON m.item_id = oi.item_id JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = m.restaurant_id WHERE o.order_status = 'Delivered' AND m.is_veg = 1
notes: four-table join through the order_items bridge table

question: How many orders are there in each order status?
gold_sql: SELECT order_status, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY order_status

question: What is the average menu item price in each category, rounded to two decimals? Show the category name and the average.
gold_sql: SELECT c.category_name, ROUND(AVG(m.price), 2) FROM menu_items m JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = m.category_id GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name
notes: rounded to 2 decimals in the question to avoid float-precision ambiguity

question: How many menu items does each restaurant have? Show the restaurant name and the count.
gold_sql: SELECT r.name, COUNT(*) FROM menu_items m JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = m.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name
notes: every restaurant has at least one menu item

question: How many ratings has each restaurant received? Show the restaurant name and the number of ratings.
gold_sql: SELECT r.name, COUNT(*) FROM ratings g JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = g.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name
notes: every restaurant has at least one rating, so an inner join loses no restaurant

question: How many status updates have been recorded for each tracking status?
gold_sql: SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM order_tracking GROUP BY status

question: What is the total revenue from delivered orders?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(final_amount) FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'Delivered'
notes: convention: revenue = final_amount (after discount), counting Delivered orders only; not total_amount and not payments.amount

question: What is the average customer rating of each restaurant, rounded to two decimals? Use the individual customer ratings, not the stored restaurant rating. Show the restaurant name and the average.
gold_sql: SELECT r.name, ROUND(AVG(g.rating), 2) FROM ratings g JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = g.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name
notes: convention: restaurant rating = AVG(ratings.rating); restaurants.avg_rating is a stored value that disagrees with it

question: Which customers placed more than 3 orders that were not cancelled? Show the customer's full name and the number of those orders.
gold_sql: SELECT c.full_name, COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE o.order_status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.full_name HAVING COUNT(*) > 3
notes: convention: cancelled orders are excluded from order counts when the question says so

question: What is the total amount of successful payments for delivered orders?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(p.amount) FROM payments p JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id WHERE p.payment_status = 'Success' AND o.order_status = 'Delivered'
notes: convention: a payment counts only when payment_status = 'Success'

question: What is the total discount amount given for each coupon code, counting only orders that used a coupon?
gold_sql: SELECT cp.coupon_code, SUM(o.discount_amount) FROM orders o JOIN coupons cp ON cp.coupon_id = o.coupon_id GROUP BY cp.coupon_id, cp.coupon_code
notes: convention: an order used a coupon when orders.coupon_id is not NULL

question: How many delivered orders were placed with a restaurant located in a different city from the city of the order's delivery address?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = o.restaurant_id JOIN customer_addresses a ON a.address_id = o.address_id WHERE o.order_status = 'Delivered' AND r.city <> a.city
notes: compares restaurants.city with the city of the order's delivery address (orders.address_id), not the customer's default address

question: Which restaurants have an average customer rating lower than the average of all ratings in the ratings table? Show the restaurant name and its average rating rounded to two decimals.
gold_sql: SELECT r.name, ROUND(AVG(t.rating), 2) FROM ratings t JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = t.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name HAVING AVG(t.rating) < (SELECT AVG(rating) FROM ratings)
notes: overall average is taken over all ratings rows (not the mean of restaurant averages); restaurant rating uses ratings, not restaurants.avg_rating

question: List the full names of customers who have never placed an order.
gold_sql: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.order_id IS NULL
notes: anti-join; exactly one customer qualifies

question: List the item name and restaurant name of every menu item that has never been ordered.
gold_sql: SELECT m.item_name, r.name FROM menu_items m JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = m.restaurant_id WHERE m.item_id NOT IN (SELECT item_id FROM order_items)
notes: anti-join through the order_items bridge; order status is not considered (any order line counts as ordered)

question: For each category, how many different restaurants offer at least one available menu item? Show the category name and the number of restaurants.
gold_sql: SELECT c.category_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.restaurant_id) FROM menu_items m JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = m.category_id WHERE m.is_available = 1 GROUP BY c.category_id, c.category_name
notes: COUNT(DISTINCT restaurant_id): a restaurant with several available items in a category counts once; 'available' = menu_items.is_available = 1

question: Which five restaurants have the largest total quantity of items ordered in orders that were not cancelled? Show the restaurant name and the total quantity, largest first.
gold_sql: SELECT r.name, SUM(oi.quantity) FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = o.restaurant_id WHERE o.order_status <> 'Cancelled' GROUP BY r.restaurant_id, r.name ORDER BY SUM(oi.quantity) DESC LIMIT 5
notes: quantity summed over order lines (not number of lines); top 5 are distinct (65, 64, 62, 57, 47) and the sixth (45) is lower, so the order and the cut are unambiguous

question: What is the total discount amount of the orders that contain at least one vegetarian menu item?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(o.discount_amount) FROM orders o WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_items oi JOIN menu_items m ON m.item_id = oi.item_id WHERE oi.order_id = o.order_id AND m.is_veg = 1)
notes: fan-out trap: an order with several vegetarian lines must have its discount counted once

question: What is the revenue of each cuisine type? Show the cuisine type and its revenue, highest first.
gold_sql: SELECT r.cuisine_type, SUM(o.final_amount) FROM orders o JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = o.restaurant_id WHERE o.order_status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY r.cuisine_type ORDER BY SUM(o.final_amount) DESC
notes: revenue per the semantic layer (delivered orders, final_amount); all cuisine revenues distinct (verified)

question: How many orders have an 'Out for Delivery' entry in their tracking history but a current order status other than 'Out for Delivery'?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o WHERE o.order_status <> 'Out for Delivery' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM order_tracking t WHERE t.order_id = o.order_id AND t.status = 'Out for Delivery')
notes: distinguishes orders.order_status (current status) from order_tracking.status (history)

question: How many delivered orders were placed on a Saturday or a Sunday?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'Delivered' AND strftime('%w', order_date) IN ('0', '6')
notes: order_date is text 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'; weekday via strftime('%w') (0 = Sunday, 6 = Saturday)

question: How many customers placed at least one order in 2024 and at least one order in 2025?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id HAVING SUM(strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2024') > 0 AND SUM(strftime('%Y', order_date) = '2025') > 0)
notes: orders of any status; calendar years of orders.order_date

question: For each restaurant, what is its most expensive menu item? Show the restaurant name, the item name and the price.
gold_sql: SELECT r.name, m.item_name, m.price FROM menu_items m JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = m.restaurant_id WHERE m.price = (SELECT MAX(m2.price) FROM menu_items m2 WHERE m2.restaurant_id = m.restaurant_id)
notes: greatest-per-group; the maximum price is unique within every restaurant (verified)

question: For each restaurant city, what is the average customer rating across all ratings of the restaurants in that city, rounded to one decimal?
gold_sql: SELECT r.city, ROUND(AVG(t.rating), 1) FROM ratings t JOIN restaurants r ON r.restaurant_id = t.restaurant_id GROUP BY r.city
notes: average over individual rating rows of each city's restaurants (not an average of restaurant averages); city is restaurants.city; rounded to one decimal because Kolkata's average is exactly 4.125, a two-decimal rounding tie

question: Which coupon code generated the highest revenue? Show the coupon code and its revenue.
gold_sql: SELECT c.coupon_code, SUM(o.final_amount) FROM orders o JOIN coupons c ON c.coupon_id = o.coupon_id WHERE o.order_status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY c.coupon_id, c.coupon_code ORDER BY SUM(o.final_amount) DESC LIMIT 1
notes: revenue per the semantic layer, attributed to the coupon used; the maximum is unique (verified)

question: What is the total amount of payments that were refunded for orders that used a coupon?
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(p.amount) FROM payments p JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = p.order_id WHERE p.payment_status = 'Refunded' AND o.coupon_id IS NOT NULL
notes: payments.amount of Refunded payments, restricted to orders with coupon_id IS NOT NULL

question: List the full names of customers who gave at least one rating below 3 and who also have at least one cancelled order.
gold_sql: SELECT c.full_name FROM customers c WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM ratings t WHERE t.customer_id = c.customer_id AND t.rating < 3) AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders o WHERE o.customer_id = c.customer_id AND o.order_status = 'Cancelled')
notes: two independent existence conditions on different tables; each customer listed once

question: For each delivery-partner vehicle type, how many delivered orders were handled by partners with that vehicle type? Show the vehicle type and the number of orders.
gold_sql: SELECT d.vehicle_type, COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN delivery_partners d ON d.partner_id = o.delivery_partner_id WHERE o.order_status = 'Delivered' GROUP BY d.vehicle_type
notes: orders.delivery_partner_id -> delivery_partners.partner_id (different column names)

question: How many customers have placed more orders than the average number of orders per customer, where the average is taken only over customers who have placed at least one order? Count orders of every status.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT customer_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id) WHERE n > (SELECT AVG(n2) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n2 FROM orders GROUP BY customer_id))
notes: aggregate over an aggregate; the average is not an integer

question: How many orders used a coupon on a date outside the coupon's validity period, that is, before its valid-from date or after its valid-to date?
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders o JOIN coupons c ON c.coupon_id = o.coupon_id WHERE DATE(o.order_date) < c.valid_from OR DATE(o.order_date) > c.valid_to
notes: orders of any status; the order date (date part of orders.order_date) is compared with coupons.valid_from / valid_to; no order falls on a boundary day, so inclusive/exclusive reading does not matter

question: What is the average final amount of delivered orders that used a coupon? Round to two decimals.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(final_amount), 2) FROM orders WHERE order_status = 'Delivered' AND coupon_id IS NOT NULL
notes: coupon usage = orders.coupon_id IS NOT NULL (semantic layer); final_amount is the post-discount amount
